summary: Optional sources are finished, and none of them is mounted in the app yet; ui-integration will mount them using CONTRACT §12.3. All three sources work with free, official or officially sanctioned access, with no keys or accounts. (1) Official evacuation zones: WORKING, current status only. They come from Cal OES's public 'California Evacuation Aggregation Layer', which combines county GIS services and Genasys Protect and is rebuilt every 5 minutes. A second Cal OES layer, the County Evacuation Inventory, says which counties feed it. Official wording is kept verbatim, and the issuing authority, the issuer's update time and Cal OES's disclaimer travel with every answer. Any time before now minus 6 h, and any historical replay, gets 'not available for past dates' rather than today's status. (2) Public cameras: WORKING, live only. Camera locations come from Cal OES's public 'California Webcams' layer, covering ALERTCalifornia wildfire cameras (UC San Diego, CC BY-NC-ND) and Caltrans CCTV (public domain). Caltrans status comes from the official CWWP2 feeds. An image is fetched only on an explicit 'Show latest image' click, shown uncropped with its credit, licence and the camera server's Last-Modified time. Nothing autoplays or auto-refreshes. (3) Recent satellite imagery: WORKING, for live and past dates. Sources are Sentinel-2 L2A scenes from the Element 84 Earth Search STAC, which Fire-3d renders into an exactly aligned Web Mercator image; Landsat HLS L30, VIIRS daily and GOES-West GeoColor come as NASA GIBS tiles, with pass times from NASA CMR. Each image carries its acquisition time, latency, resolution, cloud cover and coverage. Blocked and not used: direct Genasys Protect (needs a subscription agreement, though its zones already reach us through Cal OES), ALERTWildfire/UNR cameras (terms not verified, plain-HTTP images), and parsing CAL FIRE incident pages (free text, no zones). The backend is backend/fire3d/api/extras.py: 7 endpoints under /api/extras/, built on fire3d.http with per-source caching and rate limits, plus 39 offline pytest tests. The frontend is web/src/extras/**: typed clients and hooks, MapLibre layer handles that survive basemap swaps, cross-hatched zone styles in the CONTRACT §9 colours, legend entries, three panels with honest loading, unavailable and past-date states, feed items (evacuation, camera, imagery), and credits. It has 61 vitest tests. Each source is proven on the dev-only page web/extras-dev.html, which is not a build input. This session I resumed after the pause, finished the security sweep (no HTML sinks, no secret anywhere, https-only links), ran every check, smoke-tested all endpoints live again, and added one clarifying paragraph about import paths to CONTRACT §12.3.

contract_deviations: The envelope uses epoch milliseconds (`retrieved_ms`, `source_updated_ms`, `requested_at_ms`, `now_ms`), following SPEC's time convention, rather than the task's wording `retrieved_at`. The status values are exactly available / unavailable / not_available_for_past_dates, plus a machine `reason_code`.

Rule for 'past': a requested time older than now minus 6 h (the timeline's STALE_AFTER), or any historical incident, counts as past and gets not_available_for_past_dates. In live mode, the timeline NOW marker and anything after it count as the present even when the latest observation is stale (Cooley's NOW marker is 14 h old). The NOW view of a live fire therefore shows current status, clearly labelled 'Shown as current status' with fetch times.

Evacuation colours follow CONTRACT §9 (order #e0459b, warning #a78bfa, other #7aa2f7) with cross-hatching, not Cal OES's own red/yellow/purple symbology, because red, orange and yellow mean fire information here (BRIEF §5).

Additions beyond 'list scenes or tile layers': Fire-3d renders Sentinel-2 true-colour COGs into an exactly aligned Web Mercator WebP (`/api/extras/imagery/sentinel2.webp`, disk cache in data/cache/extras/sentinel2 capped at 300 MB). Camera frames are proxied: content-addressed, in memory for at most 10 min, never on disk. This keeps the shown time equal to the bytes' Last-Modified and means no arbitrary URL is ever fetched.

CONTRACT.md: only section 12 was written. This session I added one paragraph to §12.3 about where to import components from: panels and ExtrasLegend come from their .tsx files, index.ts exports only non-component code, and the mount*Layer functions wrap LayerGroupHandle.
known_issues: Evacuation coverage is only as good as the counties feeding the Cal OES layer. Counties outside it get 'unavailable / not covered', or a caveat when they are partly covered.

The Cal OES layer still lists 8 Tulare County 'Evacuation Order' zones from the 2023 floods. Fire-3d shows them verbatim, with their event type and issuer time when one is given, because only the issuer can lift an order.
Many zones carry no issuer update time; the Orange County order seen in the smoke test is one. The panel then shows only Cal OES's layer edit time and Fire-3d's fetch time.
While Cal OES rebuilds the layer every 5 minutes it can briefly miss zones. The backend confirms a sudden drop before accepting it (tested), and the panel carries a caveat.
Camera pointing directions are the PTZ azimuth as last reported, not live.
ALERTWildfire (UNR) cameras listed in the Cal OES layer are excluded and counted in `excluded`.
ALERTCalifornia images are CC BY-NC-ND: non-commercial use only, and never crop them. If Fire-3d is ever used commercially, it needs a UC San Diego OIC licence.

A first (cold) Sentinel-2 render takes about 14 s; after that it comes from the cache. Fire-3d limits itself to 8 renders/min. VIIRS is 375 m and GOES is coarse, so both are context only. The panel states each resolution.

In live mode at the NOW marker, imagery lists images acquired up to the real present. For a stale live fire, the default image can therefore be newer than the marker (NOAA-21 14:30 PDT vs a 04:06 PDT marker). It is labelled with its own acquisition time, and the panel heading says 'Images acquired up to now'.

notes_for_integrator:
1. **Start with CONTRACT §12.** §12.1 covers the endpoints, §12.2 the time rules, §12.3 mounting step by step, §12.4 presentation rules, §12.5 required credits and terms, and §12.7 the dev page. Nothing is mounted yet.
2. **Data.** Use the `useEvacuations`, `useCameras` and `useImagery` hooks with `incidentAreaBbox(summary, manifest, DEFAULT_MARGIN_KM[k])` and `extrasAtMs(k, mode, timeMs, now, nowMarkerMs(manifest, forecast))`. `nowMarkerMs` is in state/store.ts. The hooks fetch only while the layer toggle is on: MapLayerKey evacuation / cameras / recentImagery.
3. **Map.** Inside map-core's controller, mount in this order: `mountImageryLayer`, then `mountEvacuationLayer`, then `mountCameraLayer`. Pass `beforeId: drapedLayers().map(l => l.id)` and `topBeforeId: topLayers().map(l => l.id)` from map/layers.ts, and call `remove()` before `map.remove()`. The handles re-add themselves after basemap swaps.
   - map-core's click handler must skip camera icons (`CAMERA_INTERACTIVE_LAYERS`; one line in §12.3).
4. **Panels and legend** come from their own files: EvacuationPanel.tsx, CameraPanel.tsx and ImageryPanel.tsx, and `ExtrasLegend` from ExtrasCommon.tsx. Import extras.css once. Replace MapLegend's 'not available (no source connected yet)' paragraph with `evacuationLegend`, `cameraLegend` and `imageryLegend`.
5. **Feed:** pass a memoised `[...evacuationFeedItems, ...cameraFeedItems, ...imageryFeedItems]` as UpdatesFeed `extraItems`.
6. **Credits:** append `evacuationCredits`, `cameraCredits` and `imageryCredits` to MapAttribution as text while each layer is visible. ALERTCalifornia's credit must sit with every image (CameraPanel already does this).
7. **Location card (optional):** `zonesAtPoint(evac.data, lon, lat)` lists the official zones at a selected point. It is empty unless the status is available, so never in replay.
8. **Dev page and handles:** `cd web && VITE_API_TARGET=http://localhost:<api> PORT=<vite> npm run dev`, then open `/extras-dev.html?preset=cooley|bryson|eaton|palisades`. `window.__extrasDev` offers setLayers, selectProduct, selectCamera, requestFrame, fitZones, view, setOpacity and state(). Start the API with FIRE3D_LIVE=0. The Bryson preset has no bundle and shows zones only when that area has current orders; they were lifted by 18:48 PDT today.
9. **Upstream politeness is built in:** caching follows each source's cadence (Cal OES 2 min, catalogue 30 min near now and 30 days for the past), with per-source limits (Cal OES 60/min, Caltrans 20, frames 30, Earth Search 30, CMR 60, GIBS 30, renders 8). Please don't add prefetch loops; camera frames must stay behind an explicit click.
10. **Processes:** I started only the API on 8716 and Vite on 5185, and stopped both. I touched no other process.
